questions.question: A certain sum of money is given at a certain rate of simple interest for 6 years. Had it been given at 7% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹1,512 more. Find the sum (in ₹).
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money is given at a certain rate of simple interest for 6 years. Had it been given at 7% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹1,512 more. Find the sum (in ₹).
questions.solution:
Let the sum be P.

SI for increased rate = ₹1,512

Increased rate = (Rate + 7)%

Difference in SI = (P × 7 × 6) / 100

⇒ ₹1,512 = (P × 42) / 100

⇒ P = 3600

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers. I. Two successive discounts of 15% and 20% II. Successive discount of 25 % and 10% III. A discount of 33% The selling price will be minimum under the scheme:
questions.questionHtml:
A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers.
I. Two successive discounts of 15% and 20%
II. Successive discount of 25 % and 10%
III. A discount of 33%
The selling price will be minimum under the scheme:
questions.solution:
Final Price after successive discounts = Original Price × (1 - Discount1) × (1 - Discount2)

Let the original price be 100 units.

For scheme I: Two successive discounts of 15% and 20%

Final Price = 100 × (1 - 0.15) × (1 - 0.20)

Final Price = 68 units

For scheme II: Successive discount of 25% and 10%

Final Price = 100 × (1 - 0.25) × (1 - 0.10)

Final Price = 67.5 units

For scheme III: A discount of 33%

Final Price = 100 × (1 - 0.33)

Final Price = 67 units

The selling price will be minimum under scheme III, which gives a final price of 67 units.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 48 m. If the length is 6 m more than the breadth, the area (in m 2 ) of the garden is:
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 48 m. If the length is 6 m more than the breadth, the area (in m<sup>2</sup>) of the garden is:
questions.solution:
Perimeter = 2(L + B)

48 = 2(B + 6 + B)

4B = 36

B = 9,L = 15,

Area = L × B, Area = 15 × 9

Area = 135 m2

questions.question: If three cubes of volume 512 cm 3 each are joined end to end, find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.
questions.questionHtml: If three cubes of volume 512 cm<sup>3</sup> each are joined end to end, find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.
questions.solution:
Volume of each cube = 512 cm3

 

a3 = 512, a = 8 cm

 

l = 3a = 24 cm, w = a = 8 cm, h = a = 8 cm

 

Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh)

 

= 2(24×8 + 24×8 + 8×8)

 

 

= 2 × 448

 

= 896 cm2

questions.question: A number r when divided by 8 leaves remainder 3. What will be the remainder when (r 2 +6r + 7) is divided by 8?
questions.questionHtml: A number r when divided by 8 leaves remainder 3. What will be the remainder when (r<sup>2</sup> +6r + 7) is divided by 8?
questions.solution:
r = 8k + 3 for some integer k

We need to find the remainder of  (r2 + 6r + 7) when divided by 8.

Substitute r = 3

( r2 = 32 = 9 )

6r = 6 × 3 = 18

Hence, (r2 + 6r + 7) = 9 + 18 + 7 = 34 

Now, divide 34 by 8

34 ÷ 8 = 4 remainder 2

questions.question: \(\text{If } \sec(t) = \frac{x}{y}, \text{ then } \cot(t) \text{ is equal to:}\)
questions.questionHtml: \(\text{If } \sec(t) = \frac{x}{y}, \text{ then } \cot(t) \text{ is equal to:}\)
questions.solution:
From sec(t) = x/y:

Hypotenuse = x, Base = y

Using Pythagoras theorem:

Perpendicular = √(Hypotenuse2 - Base2)

⇒ Perpendicular = √(x2 - y2)

cot(t) = Base / Perpendicular

⇒ cot(t) = y / √(x2 - y2)

questions.question: In a constituency, 45% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 60% of the males are illiterate and 60% of the females are literate, then by what per cent is the number of illiterate females more than that of literate males? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: In a constituency, 45% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 60% of the males are illiterate and 60% of the females are literate, then by what per cent is the number of illiterate females more than that of literate males? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
The percentage difference between illiterate females and literate males is given by:

\( \frac{\text{Illiterate females} - \text{Literate males}}{\text{Literate males}} \times 100 \)

Calculations:

Let the total number of voters be \( V \) (in arbitrary units).

The number of males = \( 0.45V \) and the number of females = \( 0.55V \).

The number of illiterate males = \( 60\% of males = 0.60 \times 0.45V = 0.27V \).

The number of illiterate females = \( 40\% of females = 0.40 \times 0.55V = 0.22V \).

The number of literate males = \( 40\% of males = 0.40 \times 0.45V = 0.18V \).

The number of literate females = \( 60\% of females = 0.60 \times 0.55V = 0.33V \).

According to the question,

\( \frac{0.22V - 0.18V}{0.18V} \times 100 = \frac{0.04V}{0.18V} \times 100 \)

\( \frac{0.04}{0.18} \times 100 \approx 22.22\% \)

questions.question: The sum of five consecutive numbers is 80. Find the largest number.
questions.questionHtml: The sum of five consecutive numbers is 80. Find the largest number.
questions.solution:
Sum = (n-2) + (n-1) + n + (n+1) + (n+2)

⇒ Sum = 5n

Given Sum = 80

⇒ 5n = 80

⇒ n = 16

The five consecutive numbers are 14, 15, 16, 17, 18.

The largest number = 18

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold \(\frac{5}{8}\) of his articles at a gain of 20% and the remaining at the cost price. What is his gain percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper sold \(\frac{5}{8}\) of his articles at a gain of 20% and the remaining at the cost price. What is his gain percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
Let cost price of 8 articles be 8 units.

 

CP of (5/8) articles = 5 units, SP of (5/8) articles at 20% gain = 5 × 1.2 = 6 units

 

CP of (3/8) articles = 3 units, SP of (3/8) articles at cost price = 3 units

 

Total SP = 6 + 3 = 9 units, Total CP = 8 units

 

Gain = 9 - 8 = 1 unit, Gain% = (1/8) × 100 = 12.5%.

questions.question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 60 hours while pipe Y can fill the tank in 72 hours. Both pipes are opened together for 20 hours. How much of the tank is left empty?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe X can fill a tank in 60 hours while pipe Y can fill the tank in 72 hours. Both pipes are opened together for 20 hours. How much of the tank is left empty?
questions.solution:
Part of tank filled by X in 1 hour = 1/60, Part of tank filled by Y in 1 hour = 1/72

Part of tank filled by both in 1 hour = (1/60) + (1/72) = (6/360) + (5/360) = 11/360

Part of tank filled in 20 hours = 20 × (11/360) = 220/360 = 11/18

Part of tank left empty = 1 - (11/18) = (18/18) - (11/18) = 7/18

questions.question: The following table shows the expenditures (in thousands of rupees) of a company in different categories from 2015 to 2019: Year Salary Fuel and Transport Bonus Interest on loans Taxes 2015 288 98 3 23.4 83 2016 343 112 2.52 32.5 108 2017 324 101 3.84 41.6 74 2018 336 133 3.68 36.4 88 2019 420 142 3.96 49.6 98 What is the average amount (in ₹) paid by the company on fuel and transport per year from 2015 to 2019?
questions.questionHtml:
The following table shows the expenditures (in thousands of rupees) of a company in different categories from 2015 to 2019:

 Year  Salary Fuel and Transport Bonus Interest on loans Taxes
2015 288 98 3 23.4 83
2016 343 112 2.52 32.5 108
2017 324 101 3.84 41.6 74
2018 336 133 3.68 36.4 88
2019 420 142 3.96 49.6 98
 

What is the average amount (in ₹) paid by the company on fuel and transport per year from 2015 to 2019?
questions.solution:
Average = (Sum of all expenditures) ÷ (Number of years)

Step 1: Add all expenditures

98 + 112 + 101 + 133 + 142 = 586

Step 2: Divide the sum by 5 (number of years)

Average = 586 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 117.2

questions.question: In 2010, a company’s total expenditure was categorised under different expense heads, and their percentage distribution is illustrated in the bar graph given below. If the expenditure on an advertisement is ₹2.1 crore, then the difference between the expenditure on transport and taxes is?
questions.questionHtml:
In 2010, a company’s total expenditure was categorised under different expense heads, and their percentage distribution is illustrated in the bar graph given below.

If the expenditure on an advertisement is ₹2.1 crore, then the difference between the expenditure on transport and taxes is?
questions.solution:
Total Expenditure = ₹2.1 crore ÷ (15 ÷ 100)

⇒ Total Expenditure = ₹14 crore

Expenditure on Transport = ₹14 crore × (12.5 ÷ 100)

⇒ Expenditure on Transport = ₹1.75 crore

Expenditure on Taxes = ₹14 crore × (10 ÷ 100)

⇒ Expenditure on Taxes = ₹1.4 crore

Difference = Expenditure on Transport - Expenditure on Taxes

⇒ Difference = ₹1.75 crore - ₹1.4 crore

⇒ Difference = ₹0.35 crore

questions.question: At what angle \(\theta\) , the value of sin ( \(\theta\) ) and cos ( \(\theta\) ) will have the same value?
questions.questionHtml: At what angle \(\theta\) , the value of sin (\(\theta\)) and cos (\(\theta\)) will have the same value?
questions.solution:
We know that:

sin(θ) = cos(θ)

⇒ sin(θ) / cos(θ) = 1

⇒ tan(θ) = 1

θ = 45º

The correct answer is option 1, 45º.

questions.question: The given table shows the number of televisions that were sold by different showrooms in years 2015 to 2019. Year/Showroom A B C D 2015 212 200 205 208 2016 210 215 225 220 2017 190 204 212 205 2018 198 212 222 224 2019 218 192 205 203 Find the difference between the sale of televisions from showrooms A, B and C in 2017 and the sale of televisions from showrooms B, C and D in 2019?
questions.questionHtml:
The given table shows the number of televisions that were sold by different showrooms in years 2015 to 2019.
Year/Showroom A B C D
2015 212 200 205 208
2016 210 215 225 220
2017 190 204 212 205
2018 198 212 222 224
2019 218 192 205 203
Find the difference between the sale of televisions from showrooms A, B and C in 2017 and the sale of televisions from showrooms B, C and D in 2019?
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of televisions sold:

Year Showroom A Showroom B Showroom C Showroom D
2017 190 204 212 205
2019 218 192 205 203

Formula used:

Difference = (Sales of A + B + C in 2017) - (Sales of B + C + D in 2019)

Calculations:

Sales of A, B, and C in 2017:

190 + 204 + 212 = 606

Sales of B, C, and D in 2019:

192 + 205 + 203 = 600

Difference:

606 - 600 = 6

∴ The difference between the sales is 6 televisions.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AOC is the diameter. B is a point on the circumference of the circle such that arc AB is (1/5) of the arc BC. What is the degree measure of \(\angle\) BOC?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AOC is the diameter. B is a point on the circumference of the circle such that arc AB is (1/5) of the arc BC. What is the degree measure of \(\angle\)BOC?
questions.solution:
The central angle subtended by an arc is directly proportional to its arc length.

Given the ratio of Arc AB to Arc BC is 1 : 5, the ratio of their central angles ∠AOB : ∠BOC is also 1 : 5.

Since AOC is a diameter, the total angle on the straight line is 180°.

∠BOC = [5 ÷ (1 + 5)] × 180°

∠BOC = (5 ÷ 6) × 180° = 150°.

∴ The correct answer is 150°.

questions.question: Study the given pie chart and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The given pie chart shows the sales of different fruits in a day for a shop. If the total number of fruits sold by a fruit seller in a day is 1200, then the number of bananas sold is ___.
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie chart and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The given pie chart shows the sales of different fruits in a day for a shop.
If the total number of fruits sold by a fruit seller in a day is 1200, then the number of bananas sold is ___.
questions.solution:
Given:

Total number of fruits sold in a day: 1,200

Percentage of bananas sold: 40%

Formula used:

Number of bananas sold = Total fruits sold × (Percentage of bananas ÷ 100)

Calculations:

Number of bananas sold = 1,200 × (40 ÷ 100)

⇒ Number of bananas sold = 1,200 × 0.40

⇒ Number of bananas sold = 480

∴ The number of bananas sold is 480.

questions.question: A circular arc whose radius is 24 cm makes an angle of 60° at the centre. The perimeter of the sector formed is: (Use π = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml:
A circular arc whose radius is 24 cm makes an angle of 60° at the centre. The perimeter of the sector formed is:
(Use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Perimeter of the sector = Length of the arc + 2 × Radius

Length of the arc = (θ/360) × 2πr

Length of the arc = (60/360) × 2π × 24

⇒ Length of the arc = 25.12 cm

Perimeter of the sector = Length of the arc + 2 × Radius

⇒ Perimeter of the sector = 25.12 + 2 × 24

⇒ Perimeter of the sector = 73.12 cm

questions.question: If 3 sin A + 4 cos A = 5, then the value of tan A is:
questions.questionHtml: If 3 sin A + 4 cos A = 5, then the value of tan A is:
questions.solution:
Given: 3 sin A + 4 cos A = 5

 

Let sin A = x and cos A = y

 

3x + 4y = 5 and x2 + y2 = 1

 

x = 3/5 and y = 4/5

 

tan A = sin A / cos A = (3/5) / (4/5)

 

tan A = 3/4

 

The value of tan A is 3/4

questions.question: A motorboat travelling at some speed can cover 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 hours. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.questionHtml: A motorboat travelling at some speed can cover 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 hours. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.solution:
Let downstream speed = D and upstream speed = U.

We have: 24/U + 40/D = 17  and  12/U + 32/D = 10.

Double the 2nd equation and subtract the 1st: 24/D = 3 ⇒ D = 8 km/h.

Substitute D = 8 in 1st equation: 24/U + 5 = 17 ⇒ U = 2 km/h.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (8 − 2) ÷ 2 = 3 km/h.

questions.question: If ∆ABC and ∆QPR are congruent triangles such that AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm, ∠B = 65° and ∠C = 75°, then which of the following is true?
questions.questionHtml: If ∆ABC and ∆QPR are congruent triangles such that AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm, ∠B = 65° and ∠C = 75°, then which of the following is true?

options.html: ∠R = 75° and ​PQ = 8 cm
∠Q = 40° and ​RQ = 7 cm
AC = PR and ∠P = 65°

questions.solution:
Since ∆ABC ≅ ∆QPR, the corresponding sides and angles will be equal. Hence, we identify the corresponding parts:

AB corresponds to PQ, AC corresponds to PR, and BC corresponds to QR.

Also, ∠A corresponds to ∠Q, ∠B corresponds to ∠P, and ∠C corresponds to ∠R.

Given AB = 7 cm, so PQ = 7 cm.

Given AC = 8 cm, so PR = 8 cm.

Given ∠C = 75º, so ∠R = 75º.

Thus, the correct option is:

PQ = 7 cm and ∠R = 75º
